answer: A staking bond resists Sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, like a grove where every tree must put down roots before bearing fruit. A prism of reputation then refracts that stake across past trades, so new identities start dim while proven ones shine. An attacker who wants a terrace of fake accounts must fund every one, and misbehavior slashes the bond, making mass fakery expensive while honest newcomers pay only a temporary lock.
